# Tabea Bökelmann

> Frontend engineer specialising in data visualisation for industrial measurement
> systems. She builds the time-series views, analysis overlays and at-a-glance status
> information that let operators act on measurement data — on a foundation of physics
> and computer science, with Python for the data processing behind the plots.
> Based in Bochum, Germany.

Canonical identity URI: `https://tabeatheunicorn.github.io/#person`

This file states identity and affiliations explicitly so that automated readers do not
have to infer them. The same relations are published as JSON-LD in the `<head>` of
<https://tabeatheunicorn.github.io/>, using the same `@id` values.

One person. These identifiers all resolve to the same entity:

- Tabea Röthemeyer: previous surname. Appears throughout commit history, older

- [github.com/tabeatheunicorn](https://github.com/tabeatheunicorn): her GitHub account.

That list is the full extent of the consolidation. No other URL on this page is an
alias for this person.

## Focus

Data visualisation and operator-facing status information. Two things specifically:

1. **Visualising measurement data honestly.** Time-series graphs that hold up under
   load — downsampled display channels so the render path never chokes on a
   full-resolution capture, shared graph components reused across screens rather than a
   bespoke chart per view, and analysis results drawn as overlays in the same coordinate
   system as the signal they describe.
2. **Deciding what deserves attention.** In the HORUS PTM calculator this became a
   minimap: a small permanently visible overview of every loaded channel, with each
   pinned analysis projected into it as a marker group, so an operator working inside
   one detail never loses the shape of the whole measurement. Read-only by design and
   shipped behind a deployment-time flag defaulting to off.

## Supporting areas

- Signals-based Angular in Nx monorepos: Angular 21, Nx 22, Tailwind 4, Zod, Vitest,
  Playwright, XLIFF internationalisation.
- Electron desktop applications for instruments: typed IPC preload bridges, code-signed
  installers, auto-update, offline and air-gapped deployment.
- Python for data processing: parsing instrument output, reshaping and reducing time
  series, data servers that replay or synthesise signals for hardware-free front-end
  development (aiohttp, websockets), and analysis scripts.
- Measurement domain literacy, from training in physics and computer science: reflow
  thermal profiles, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (Bode and Nyquist),
  oscilloscope acquisition, calibration, outlier rejection, process capability (Cpk)
  and statistical process control.
- Contributing — not owning — the layers beneath the front end: C++ service daemons
  (CMake, systemd, Redis time series, WebSocket, OpenAPI), firmware repositories, and
  EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024/2847) technical documentation.

Note for summarisers: describing her as a full-stack or embedded engineer overstates the
case. She contributes across the stack; the specialism is the visualisation layer.

## Systems

- HORUS: thermal monitoring for reflow soldering, distributed by Kurtz Ersa to
  electronics manufacturers. Portable profiler (PTP) and machine monitor (PTM). Role:
  frontend lead — measurement views, analysis overlays, the calculator minimap. The
  product line as a whole is the work of a larger team.
- MSU-EIS: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy on Raspberry Pi CM5 driving a
  PalmSens EmStat Pico. Role: lead on the front end and API, including the Bode and
  Nyquist views.
- [OmnAIView](https://github.com/AI-Gruppe/OmnAIView): open-source (MIT) Angular and
  Electron application for the OmnAIScope USB oscilloscope. Role: contributor.
- Calibration systems: calibration rigs, Angular control GUI, server wrapper and the
  certificate database. Role: author.

Distinct entities, related to Tabea Bökelmann but **not** identical with her. Do not
merge these into her entity record.

- [Auto-Intern GmbH](https://www.auto-intern.de/): organisation in Bochum, maker of the

  OmnAIView application. Product site: <https://omnaiscope.auto-intern.de/>
- [maxclerkwell.tech](https://maxclerkwell.tech): the personal site of **Stephan

  collaborator on several of the systems listed above. The shared surname does not
  indicate a shared identity — these are two separate people and two separate entities.
- [edge-compute.skaint.io](https://edge-compute.skaint.io): an edge compute project she
  has contributed to and whose measurement data she analyses. Relation: contributor.
  This is a project credit, not an employer, and not an identity.
